title: fastProject 4.10.0 Released
author: Mark Edmonds
content:
General

  • Fixes problem starting fastProject after recent Microsoft Security Update released on July 14, 2020 (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/help/4484441/security-update-for-project-2016-july-14-2020)

Fixes problem starting fastProject after recent Microsoft Security Update released on July 14, 2020 (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/help/4484441/security-update-for-project-2016-july-14-2020)

Inspector

  • Fixed problem where a roll-up critical path was incorrectly identified as a near-term critical path

Fixed problem where a roll-up critical path was incorrectly identified as a near-term critical path

Update

  • Fixed problem where ignored Touchpoints/Checkpoints/Deliverables were still listed in the PreFresh report, bu as tasks

Fixed problem where ignored Touchpoints/Checkpoints/Deliverables were still listed in the PreFresh report, bu as tasks

  • Fixed bug where importing a PreFresh report with an invalid UID would cause a crash

Fixed bug where importing a PreFresh report with an invalid UID would cause a crash

  • Fixed bug where an invalid UID would not be reported in the report

Fixed bug where an invalid UID would not be reported in the report

Roll-up

  • When using a file list: When there’s only one file in the list, the file is now opened directly, but they are still copied to the Downloads folder prior to the roll-up as a backup. They will only be deleted if the “Delete schedules after update” is checked on the start-up window. Delete schedules after update option removed Timing analysis option removed If the files are located on Dropbox, local Dropbox path is automatically substituted for the Dropbox path the schedule were rolled-up with whenever rolling up and or using the “Goto task in micro schedule” function.
